title: USF Taxonomy Catalogue
purpose: Defines the classification systems (taxonomies) for USF concepts. It formalises the concepts named in the ontology into stable category families so that later vocabulary, schemas, registries, ADRs, validators, evidence envelopes, and source-import maps classify artefacts consistently. It answers what kinds of things exist and how they are grouped; it does NOT define the exact allowed field values, which belong to the future vocabulary catalogue.
normativeLanguage: Requirement words (MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY) follow BCP 14 as defined in docs/architecture/standards-profile.md section 6. Only uppercase forms are normative.
scopeNote: This artefact is a taxonomy, not a vocabulary, not a schema, not a registry, and not an ADR. It classifies; it does not enumerate final controlled values, validate shapes, index instances, or decide policy.

governance.draftMeaning: A taxonomy with status 'draft' is defined here and in force as classification guidance, but is not yet validator-enforced; this matches the standards-profile maturity ladder (documented/structured stage).
rules: Taxonomy belongs to USF semantic definitions and is high authority (rank 1).
Taxonomy classifies ontology concepts; it MUST NOT redefine them.
Taxonomy does NOT replace the ontology.
Taxonomy does NOT define every exact allowed field value.
Exact allowed values belong in the future vocabulary catalogue where appropriate.
Taxonomy categories MUST be stable and semantically named.
Taxonomy categories MUST NOT be based on migration phase.
Taxonomy changes can alter semantic meaning and MAY require ADR review.
Taxonomy removals MUST include a disposition.
Taxonomy MUST classify USF source-lineage evidence without making source lineage future authority.
Future AI agents MUST NOT invent classification categories without adding them here or recording deferred work.

taxonomyDesignPrinciples: Classify by semantic role, not by source path.
Classify by stable purpose, not by temporary migration state.
Classify provider mode separately from environment.
Classify proof claim separately from readiness summary.
Classify command separately from script path.
Classify configuration separately from environment file location.
Classify UI semantics separately from UI implementation components.
Classify generated reports separately from raw evidence.
Classify source lineage separately from target authority.
Classify observability and audit as semantic assets.
Classify future AI decisions as governed artefacts, not informal actions.
Forbidden category naming: no 'v2', 'legacy', 'old', 'new', 'temp', 'transitional', or redundant 'usf' path segments inside the usf repository.
Historical names from USF source lineage may appear only as source references or quoted evidence, not as future taxonomy categories unless explicitly justified.
taxonomyRules: Every taxonomy family MUST have an id, title, description, governed ontology concepts, classification purpose, expected consumers, and AI guidance.
Every taxonomy MUST belong to a taxonomy family.
Every taxonomy MUST identify which ontology concepts it classifies.
Every taxonomy MUST identify future vocabulary dependencies.
Every taxonomy MUST identify future schema dependencies.
Every taxonomy MUST identify source evidence relevance.
Every taxonomy MUST avoid uncontrolled synonyms.
Every taxonomy MUST declare whether categories are exclusive, non-exclusive, hierarchical, relational, or dimensional.
Every taxonomy MUST declare whether categories are stable, provisional, or deferred.
No taxonomy category SHOULD be created solely because a source path exists.
No implementation directory SHOULD become a taxonomy category without semantic rationale.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Authority and Governance
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies artefacts by their authority role and by artefact kind, anchoring every other classification to the Authority Model order.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Establish which authority level an artefact holds and what kind of artefact it is, so downstream classification and validation can apply the correct rules.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/docs/v2-foundation/v2-readiness-final-attestation.md (validators enforce, proofs are evidence, code implements)
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Determine an artefact's authority level before reasoning about it; never let a lower-authority artefact override a higher one.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Semantic Architecture
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies the rank-1 semantic building blocks (capabilities, contracts, ports, semantic dimensions) that define intended behaviour.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Group the authoritative concepts that define what the platform should do, distinct from how it is realised.
sourceLineageInputs: capability category dimension of 12 values (identity-access, authentication, entitlements-billing, events-workflow, security-governance, observability-ops, data-platform, developer-platform, compute-runtime, configuration, search, foundation)
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Treat these concepts as authoritative; the capability-domain value set is recognised from USF source lineage but its canonical USF values remain explicitly deferred in the vocabulary catalogue.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Source Lineage
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies elements of USF source lineage as evidence by kind and by the role they play, so historical knowledge is preserved without copying structure.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Make every historical element classifiable as evidence with a role and a future disposition, so no knowledge is lost and source path never dictates target architecture.
sourceLineageInputs: file disposition vocabulary of 9 historical values
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Classify a source element as evidence before importing; record a disposition; never treat the source as future authority.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Evidence and Proof
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies evidence by kind and proof by concept, keeping intended behaviour, exercised behaviour, and summaries distinct.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Separate raw, semantic, proof, normalised, report, and attestation evidence; separate proof claims from readiness summaries; keep proof honest.
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: A passing proof is evidence of fact, not a definition of intent; readiness claims MUST NOT exceed observed evidence; missing collected evidence MUST fail closed.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Provider and Environment
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies provider concepts and environment concepts as two separate first-class dimensions.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Keep provider mode (what kind of provider evidence) and environment (where it ran) distinct, and keep production-shaped distinct from production/live.
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Never infer a stronger provider mode or environment than the substrate used; hermetic mock proof is valid internal proof but not live external proof.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Command and Configuration
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies executable commands and configuration as governed semantic assets.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Treat Make targets, package scripts, CLI commands, env vars, config files, and compose settings as semantic assets that cannot be deleted or renamed without disposition.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/Makefile and make/*.mk (make all is the authoritative full-confidence command)
source-lineage/package.json (212 npm scripts incl ~110 proof:* scripts)
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Commands and configuration are semantic assets, not incidental scripts; regenerate config from manifests; never hand-edit generated config.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Interface, Event, and Workflow
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies callable contracts, events/messages, and workflows that span capabilities.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Preserve operational and integration semantics as contracts that precede or are reconciled with implementation, never inferred from code alone.
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Where a semantic interface/event contract exists, code conforms to it; do not invent routes or events in code.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Data and Migration
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies data models, persistence contracts, migrations, and backup/restore concerns.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Preserve persistence contracts, tenancy isolation, forward-only checksum-immutable migrations, and backup/restore proof relationships.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/docs/v2-foundation/data-and-migration-plan.json (PostgreSQL schema-per-tenant; RLS and rlsBypass; forward-only checksum-immutable migration chain 001..034 then 035+; backupRestore; destructiveOpControls; dataVerification)
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Never edit a committed migration; preserve tenancy invariants; classify backup and restore so emitted and collected evidence can be checked.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Observability and Audit
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies logs, metrics, traces, spans, runtime events, audit events, and correlation as semantic assets.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Support proof, debugging, accountability, and drift detection; require audit for security-sensitive and state-changing operations.
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Observability and audit are semantic assets; removal requires semantic review, never an incidental refactor.

taxonomyFamilies.title: UI Semantics
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies user-facing meaning (surfaces, journeys, states, validation, permissions, accessibility) independent of visual design.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Preserve UI behaviour and proof expectations so the visual layer can be regenerated without inventing behaviour.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/docs/v2-foundation/ui-capability-model.json (28 UI capabilities; 12 personas; routes, forms, tables, commands, states, a11y, telemetry)
rule that the generator must never read old JSX
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Visual redesign is not semantic deletion; preserve UI semantics unless changed through coupled semantic/ADR/proof/validator updates.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Implementation Realisation
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies implementation structures (apps, packages, services, adapters) without making them semantic authority.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Describe how capabilities are realised while keeping implementation structure subordinate to semantic classification.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/packages (~41 packages; core leaves domain-identity, authorisation-runtime, platform-errors, platform-runtime-context; adapters-* are the only packages permitted to import external SDKs)
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Implementation realisation is rank-5 and lower authority than semantics; a package boundary is not a capability boundary.

taxonomyFamilies.title: Validation and Reporting
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies validators, validation inputs/outputs, and generated reports.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Make validators executable enforcement that fails closed, and keep generated reports as the lowest-authority summaries.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/tools/v2-readiness (~60 rules R1-R62; fails closed; normalises no aliases; writes no runtime file; exit codes; golden and negative-control tests)
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: Validators enforce but never define product semantics; reports summarise but never override evidence or semantic definitions.

taxonomyFamilies.title: AI Governance
taxonomyFamilies.description: Classifies AI-agent-relevant artefacts and actions as governed, not informal.
taxonomyFamilies.purpose: Make AI instructions, generated and reviewed artefacts, alignment rules, forbidden inferences, conflicts, and stop conditions explicit and governed.
taxonomyFamilies.aiGuidance: An AI agent holds no authority; it is bound by the authority order and its claims are checked by validators, not trusted.

taxonomies.title: Authority Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify any governed artefact by the single authority role it holds, aligned to the Authority Model order. A given artefact holds exactly one authority role.

categories.description: Rank 1; defines intended behaviour and contract.
Rank 2; normative decision that permits or forbids and explains why.
Rank 4; execution-backed evidence of what happened.
Rank 5 source lineage consulted to recover intent.

categoryRules: Categories are exclusive: an artefact holds one authority role.
These categories mirror the Authority Model section 1 ranks; the exact value tokens used by schema fields are deferred to the authority-levels vocabulary.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/docs/v2-foundation/semantic-source-of-truth-transition.md (validators enforce; proofs are evidence; code implements canonical semantic artefacts)
validationExpectations: Once vocabulary exists, every governed artefact carries exactly one authority-level value from the authority-levels vocabulary.
driftRisks: Treating a source file or report as semantic authority.
Letting a lower rank override a higher rank.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Identify authority role first; never let rank-5/6/7 override rank-1/2.
deferredDetails: Canonical authority-level value tokens are formalised in the vocabulary authority-levels set; the catalogue header uses the canonical token semantic-definition.

taxonomies.title: Artefact Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify USF artefacts by kind so the correct future schema can validate each.

categories.description: Human-readable governance document (charter, authority model, standards profile, ontology).
This kind of artefact: classification systems.
Index/cross-reference map of concepts and artefacts.
Reference to historical or current source evidence.
Record mapping source elements to USF concepts via disposition.

categoryRules: Categories are exclusive by primary kind.
An artefact's kind selects its governing schema family.
validationExpectations: Artefact kind resolves to a known future schema.
driftRisks: Conflating a generated report with a semantic artefact.
Treating a runbook as a contract.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Classify artefact kind before choosing how to validate or author it.

taxonomies.title: Semantic Architecture Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Group the rank-1 semantic building blocks by their role in defining intended behaviour, distinct from implementation realisation.

categories.description: A normative statement of intended behaviour or structure.
A semantic boundary contract fulfilled by adapters.
User-facing meaning independent of visual design.
Provider class as a semantic dimension.
Execution context as a semantic dimension.

categoryRules: Relational: building blocks reference each other (capability is defined by contracts; ports are fulfilled by adapters).
The capability-domain value set (12 historical categories) is recognised as evidence but its canonical USF values are deferred to vocabulary.
validationExpectations: Every capability has at least one semantic contract before its implementation is authoritative.
driftRisks: Inferring a semantic building block from a folder.
Letting implementation define a contract.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Read the semantic building block before its implementation; never invent a contract from code resemblance.

taxonomies.title: Source Evidence Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify what kind of source element from USF source lineage a reference points at, so it can be carried via disposition without copying structure.

categories.description: Application or library source code file.
A machine-readable semantic definition (e.g. capability closure, operational semantics).
A data/migration plan or migration file.

categoryRules: Non-exclusive: an element may carry more than one source-evidence kind.
Source kind does not dictate target path or authority.
validationExpectations: Every source reference declares at least one source kind from the source-kinds vocabulary once it exists.
driftRisks: Deriving architecture from source path.
Losing an element by failing to classify it.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Classify before import; no source element disappears without a disposition.

taxonomies.title: Source Role Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify what a source element is used for, so its intent is preserved when promoted into USF semantics.
categoryRules: Role determines which USF semantic concept the element informs, not where its file lives.
validationExpectations: Every source reference declares at least one role.
driftRisks: Treating generated-summary-evidence as semantic-source.
Treating historical-lineage as live authority.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Use role to recover intent into USF semantics; preserve lineage citations.

taxonomies.title: Evidence Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify a piece of evidence by kind so the right handling, freshness, and authority apply.

categories.description: Evidence carried in a semantic artefact.
Raw evidence reshaped for indexing, raw retained.
A status statement referencing underlying evidence.

categoryRules: Reports and attestations are distinct from raw and proof evidence.
validationExpectations: Evidence identifies its source or generation process; generated reports reference the evidence they summarise.
driftRisks: Hiding missing raw evidence behind a green report.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Never conflate kinds; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

taxonomies.title: Proof Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify proof-related concepts so claims, execution, evidence, and readiness stay distinct. Proof LEVELS (the L0-L6 ladder) are deferred to vocabulary.

categories.description: The claim a proof asserts it exercises.
The executable that runs the proof.
A specific run of a proof.
A claim of readiness derived from proof.
A claim that foundation-level properties hold.
A condition under which the proof must fail closed.

categoryRules: Relational: claim -> script -> execution -> emitted -> collected -> normalised -> readiness.
Proof levels are NOT defined here; they are a vocabulary dependency.
validationExpectations: A proof identifies its claim, environment, and provider mode; readiness claims do not exceed observed evidence; missing emitted/collected evidence fails closed.
driftRisks: Treating a readiness-claim as observed evidence.
Overclaiming a proof level.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Never relabel a proof upward; classify claim separately from readiness summary.

taxonomies.title: Provider Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify provider concepts. Provider-mode VALUES are deferred to vocabulary.

categories.description: The declared class of provider evidence (values in vocabulary).
Implementation binding a port to a provider.
A capability's reliance on a provider.
A claim about a provider's readiness.
A declared exception in provider behaviour or policy.

categoryRules: Provider-mode VALUES (hermetic, compose-local, sandbox-external, live-external, none) are deferred to vocabulary, not enumerated here.
sourceLineageInputs: in-memory to real provider parity reports
source-lineage/services/mock-oidc; compose.yaml providers (keycloak, openbao, redis, minio, temporal, windmill, clamav, pgbackrest)
validationExpectations: A provider adapter identifies the port and provider mode it fulfils.
driftRisks: Mislabelling a hermetic provider as live.
Inferring a provider mode from the adapter name.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Record provider mode; mock/hermetic providers (including mock IdP) are valid internal proof but not live external proof.

taxonomies.title: Environment Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify environment concepts. Environment-class VALUES are deferred to vocabulary.

categories.description: The execution context in which behaviour or proof occurs.
The kind of environment (values in vocabulary).
A claim that something holds in an environment.
A claim about a production-shaped rehearsal context.
A claim about real tenant operation with live providers.
A fully isolated, deterministic, offline context.

categoryRules: Environment-class VALUES (local, hermetic, integration, staging, production-shaped, production-live) are deferred to vocabulary.
validationExpectations: Every evidence and proof claim declares its environment; environment claims do not exceed evidence.
driftRisks: Treating an environment name as a readiness claim.
Treating production-shaped as production-live.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Keep environment distinct from provider mode; never infer a stronger environment claim than evidence supports.

taxonomies.title: Command Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify executable commands by purpose, treating them as semantic assets.
categoryRules: Non-exclusive: a command may serve multiple purposes.
Classify by purpose, not by script path.
validationExpectations: A command declares purpose, environment scope, evidence outputs, and failure semantics; no command is deleted/renamed without disposition.
driftRisks: Silent loss/rename of a command.
Classifying a command by its file path only.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Commands are semantic assets, not incidental scripts.

taxonomies.title: Configuration Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify configuration by kind and relevance, treating it as a governed semantic asset.

categories.description: Selects or configures a provider/provider mode.
A setting a proof depends on.

categoryRules: Classify by meaning, not by file location.
Generated env files are projections of manifests, never authoritative.
validationExpectations: A config key declares source, requiredness, environment applicability, secret classification, provider relevance, and proof relevance.
driftRisks: Hand-editing generated config.
Misclassifying a secret-bearing setting.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Regenerate config from manifests; never hand-edit generated config; never leak secret values into evidence.

taxonomies.title: Interface Classification

categories.description: A semantic boundary to a provider.
A contract exposed to external consumers.

categoryRules: Contract-first or contract-reconciled; not inferred from handlers when a contract exists.
validationExpectations: An interface resolves to a semantic contract; runtime drift from the contract is detectable.
driftRisks: Inferring an interface from code when a contract exists.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Define or reconcile the contract first; never invent routes in code.

taxonomies.title: Event and Workflow Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify event and workflow concepts and their cross-capability roles.

categories.description: A change in a lifecycle state.

categoryRules: Event/workflow semantics (ordering, idempotency, DLQ, retention, compensation) are contract-level.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/docs/v2-foundation/cross-capability-interactions.json (8 interaction types: sync-api, event, workflow, data-reference, readiness-dependency, provider-dependency, audit-dependency, lifecycle-dependency)
validationExpectations: An event has a contract before emission; a workflow declares ordering, consistency, and compensation.
driftRisks: Inventing events in code.
Losing DLQ/ordering semantics in a refactor.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Classify the failure-path and compensation-path explicitly; do not infer them from orchestration code.
deferredDetails: event-kind value tokens (vocabulary); interaction-type value set.

taxonomies.title: Data and Migration Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify data, persistence, migration, and backup/restore concerns.

categories.description: A contract for how data is stored.
A forward-only change to data shape/structure.

categoryRules: Migrations are forward-only and checksum-immutable; committed migrations are never edited.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/docs/v2-foundation/data-and-migration-plan.json (PostgreSQL schema-per-tenant; RLS/rlsBypass; migration chain 001..034 then 035+; backupRestore; destructiveOpControls; dataVerification)
validationExpectations: Backup/restore emitted evidence is preserved through collection; missing collected evidence fails closed; committed migrations are checksum-immutable.
driftRisks: Editing a committed migration.
Tenant data leakage from broken RLS.
Hiding missing backup/restore evidence.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Preserve tenancy invariants and migration immutability; classify backup and restore evidence so it can be checked.

taxonomies.title: Observability and Audit Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify runtime observability and audit concepts as semantic assets.

categories.description: Observability output emitted by a proof.
An id linking signals across systems.
A record establishing who did what.

categoryRules: Naming/shape will be guided by an OpenTelemetry-adapted controlled vocabulary.
Audit is required for security-sensitive and state-changing operations.
sourceLineageInputs: assurance bars: 0 routes without tracing/logging/metrics; 0 mutations without audit
validationExpectations: Every mutating/privileged action has a defined audit semantic; observability supports proof and drift detection.
driftRisks: Removing a signal or audit event as an incidental refactor.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Removal of observability/audit requires semantic review, never a silent cleanup.

taxonomies.title: UI Semantic Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify user-facing meaning independent of visual implementation.

categories.description: A UI state (loading, success, auth-required, error).
Landmark, heading, accessible name, keyboard behaviour.
An action a user can take.
Mapping of a UI action to a command/query/event.
Mapping of a UI journey to an e2e proof.

categoryRules: UI semantics are derived from behaviour, never from JSX styling.
validationExpectations: A UI journey maps to capability semantics and to proof evidence where available.
driftRisks: Treating a UI component as a capability.
Deleting a journey/state/permission/a11y requirement as a restyle.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Visual redesign is not semantic deletion; preserve UI semantics through coupled updates only.

taxonomies.title: Implementation Realisation Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify implementation structures without granting them semantic authority.
categoryRules: Implementation realisation is rank-5 and lower authority than semantic classification.
A directory does not become a category without semantic rationale.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/packages (~41; adapters-* import external SDKs only)
validationExpectations: An implementation may realise multiple capabilities but must not erase their semantic boundaries.
driftRisks: Treating a package boundary as a capability boundary.
Letting code define behaviour.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Make implementation conform to semantics; never learn intent from code structure.
deferredDetails: Whether any additional implementation sub-kinds need controlled vocabulary beyond source-kinds, source-roles, and artefact-kinds.

taxonomies.title: Validation and Reporting Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify validators, their inputs/outputs, and generated reports.

categories.description: A single rule within a validator.
A report whose evidence commit no longer matches current.

categoryRules: Validators fail closed; reports are rank-7 and never override evidence.
sourceLineageInputs: source-lineage/tools/v2-readiness (R1-R62; fails closed; exit codes 0/1/2; normalises no aliases; golden and negative-control tests)
validationExpectations: A validator report identifies the evidence it summarises; staleness is detectable by commit-pin.
driftRisks: Believing a stale report.
Downgrading a blocking failure to advisory to pass.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Never weaken a rule to pass; never treat a report as canonical.

taxonomies.title: AI Governance Classification
taxonomies.purpose: Classify AI-agent-relevant artefacts and actions so AI work is governed, not informal.

categories.description: An instruction given to an AI agent.
An artefact produced by an AI agent.
An artefact reviewed by an AI agent.
A binding constraint on AI behaviour.
An inference pattern that is prohibited.
An unresolved conflict between authority sources.
A condition under which the agent must stop or fail.

categoryRules: AI actions are governed artefacts subject to the authority order.
sourceLineageInputs: docs/architecture/charter.md section 7; authority-model.md section 6; standards-profile.md section 20; ontology.md sections 14-15
validationExpectations: AI-generated artefacts carry rationale and references; forbidden inferences are detectable; stop conditions are explicit.
driftRisks: Treating AI output as authoritative without checks.
Proceeding through an unresolved authority conflict.
taxonomies.aiGuidance: Stop or fail on unresolved authority conflict; never self-grant authority.

taxonomyRelationships.statement: Authority classification applies to all governed artefacts and anchors every other taxonomy to the Authority Model order.
Artefact classification determines which future schema may validate an artefact.
Source evidence classification feeds the source-reference and import-manifest schemas.
Source role classification preserves USF source-lineage knowledge without copying structure blindly.
Evidence classification feeds the evidence-envelope and proof-evidence schemas.
Provider classification and environment classification MUST remain separate dimensions.
Proof classification depends on provider and environment classification; a proof claim is meaningless without both.
Command and configuration classifications preserve Make/env/config semantics as assets.
Interface, event, and workflow classifications preserve operational and integration semantics.
UI semantic classification preserves behaviour independently of visual redesign.
Observability and audit classification supports proof, debugging, accountability, and drift detection.
Implementation realisation classification is lower authority than semantic classification.
AI governance classification constrains future generated work.

vocabularyDependencies.statement: This taxonomy was created before the vocabulary catalogue in the foundational sequence. The current vocabulary catalogue now backs the controlled value sets listed as active below; explicitly deferred sets remain deferred and MUST NOT be treated as resolved.
vocabularyDependencies.guidance: This taxonomy guides vocabulary maintenance; future schemas SHOULD prefer vocabulary values where fields require exact allowed values.
vocabularyDependencies.doNotMarkResolved: Deferred vocabulary dependencies MUST NOT be marked resolved before their vocabulary values exist.

expectedVocabularySets.note: Recognised from the source-lineage 12-category capability dimension; canonical USF values remain deferred.

sourceLineageLearnings.learning: Source files must be classified as evidence before import.
Make targets must be classified as semantic command evidence.
Package scripts must be classified as command evidence.
Env/config files must be classified as configuration evidence.
Compose services must be classified as runtime/environment/provider evidence.
Tests and e2e journeys must be classified as behavioural/UI/proof evidence where applicable.
Proof scripts must be classified separately from generated reports.
Generated reports must be classified as lower-authority summaries.
Readiness claims must be classified separately from observed proof evidence.
Provider mode and environment must be classified separately.
Production-shaped must be classified separately from production/live.
Hermetic mock proof must be classified as valid internal proof but not live external proof.
Backup/restore evidence must be classified so emitted and collected evidence can be checked.
No source element should disappear without disposition.
Source path classification must not dictate target architecture.
UI components/pages must not automatically become capabilities without semantic mapping.
Operational semantics, event semantics, and cross-capability interactions must be classified as semantic evidence.
Source naming from USF source lineage may be historical evidence but must not force future USF naming.
The historical readiness validator fails closed, normalises no aliases, and writes no runtime file.
sourceLineageLearnings.taxonomyImpact: validation-reporting-classification; informs that controlled vocabulary (no alias normalisation) is essential

sourceLineageLearnings.learning: Capability completeness in USF source lineage drops to gap if any facet lacks authoritative backing.

externalStandardsInfluence.influence: Every family, taxonomy, and category has a stable kebab id; no migration-phase names.
Categories aim to be mutually clear; uncontrolled synonyms are forbidden; exact controlled values deferred to vocabulary.
Capabilities and bounded semantic building blocks are classified by domain meaning, not by package layout.
Implementation realisation is kept distinct from semantic architecture (analogous to separating views).
This artefact is plain JSON with no comments, trailing commas, JSON5, or YAML.
USF claims no formal taxonomy/ontology standard compliance; validators and schemas that would substantiate such a claim are deferred.

validationExpectations: Taxonomy catalogue MUST parse as JSON.
Taxonomy family ids MUST be unique.
Taxonomy ids MUST be unique.
Taxonomy ids MUST follow naming rules (no forbidden migration-phase tokens).
Taxonomy families MUST be known (drawn from taxonomyFamilies).
Every taxonomy MUST belong to a known family.
Every taxonomy MUST identify governed ontology concepts.
Every taxonomy MUST identify future vocabulary dependencies.
Every taxonomy MUST identify future schema dependencies.
Every taxonomy MUST include AI guidance.
Categories MUST NOT use forbidden migration-phase names.
Categories MUST NOT be source-path-only classifications.
Taxonomy MUST NOT silently define vocabulary-only values as final controlled values.
Taxonomy MUST NOT mark vocabulary dependencies as resolved before vocabulary exists.
Future validators MUST be able to check category references once schemas and vocabulary exist.
aiAgentRules: Read charter, authority model, standards profile, ontology, and this taxonomy before creating vocabulary, schemas, registries, ADRs, validators, import maps, or implementation.
Classify concepts before naming files or fields.
Do not create new taxonomy categories without updating this catalogue or recording deferred work.
Do not treat taxonomy categories as exact allowed field values unless backed by vocabulary.
Do not infer taxonomy from source path alone.
Do not confuse provider mode with environment.
Do not confuse generated reports with raw evidence.
Do not confuse source evidence with future authority.
Do not treat implementation structure as semantic classification.
Do not use forbidden names (v2, legacy, old, new, temp, transitional, redundant usf).
Stop or fail when ontology and taxonomy conflict.
